description.summary: let the window manager handle touchpad gestures

protocol.description:
This protocol allows the river-window-management-v1 window manager to claim multi-finger touchpad swipe and pinch gestures, for example to switch workspaces or open an overview the way desktop shells do.
Gestures are claimed by finger count. A claimed gesture is delivered to the window manager from begin to end instead of to the client with pointer focus (through zwp_pointer_gestures_v1). Gestures that are not claimed are delivered to clients as usual.
Note: this is a downstream extension maintained with the Pangolin desktop, it is not part of upstream river.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.

interface.name: river_touchpad_gestures_v1
interface.description: This global interface should only be advertised to the client if the river_window_manager_v1 global is also advertised.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request indicates that the client will no longer use the river_touchpad_gestures_v1 object.

request.name: get_seat
request.description:
Create an object to claim and receive the touchpad gestures of a seat.
It is a protocol error to make this request more than once for a given river_seat_v1 object.

interface.name: river_touchpad_gestures_seat_v1
interface.description:
Claims touchpad gestures of a seat and delivers them to the window manager.
Changing the claimed finger counts takes effect for the next gesture to begin. A gesture that already began is always delivered to whoever received its begin event.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Release all claimed gestures. A gesture in progress is ended with cancelled set for the window manager and not delivered to clients.

request.name: set_swipe_fingers

description.summary: claim swipe gestures by finger count

request.description: Claim swipe gestures performed with the given numbers of fingers, replacing any previous claim. Bit n of the mask claims swipes with n fingers, e.g. 0x18 claims 3- and 4-finger swipes. A mask of 0 claims no swipes. Initially no swipes are claimed.

arg.name: finger_mask
arg.summary: bit n set: claim n fingers

request.name: set_pinch_fingers

description.summary: claim pinch gestures by finger count

request.description: Claim pinch gestures performed with the given numbers of fingers, replacing any previous claim, with the same mask format as set_swipe_fingers. Initially no pinches are claimed.

arg.name: finger_mask
arg.summary: bit n set: claim n fingers

event.name: swipe_update
event.description: Motion since the previous swipe_begin or swipe_update event, in the same unaccelerated-but-scaled units as zwp_pointer_gestures_v1.

event.name: pinch_update
event.description: Centroid motion since the previous event, and the scale and rotation relative to the beginning of the gesture (scale starts at 1.0).
